    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/radial-4-works-best-as-an-automation-hub"/>
    <title>Radial 4 Works Best as an Automation Hub</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--png"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" alt="Radial" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBMVNNQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--475905546719757d36f756dc8270e7e8bc8301bc/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJY0c1bkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--768aeab7fb7843d85fe5b2b4ba237e06e6ef604f/UIUpdate.png" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
    &lt;figcaption class="attachment__caption text-center"&gt;
      Radial
    &lt;/figcaption&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I spent the afternoon experimenting with &lt;a href="https://radial.appverge.net/"&gt;Radial 4&lt;/a&gt;, a rapidly evolving pie-menu app from independent developer Gustav Lubker of AppVerge. If you’re not familiar with pie menu apps, they present a circular menu divided into sections (or slices), each representing an action or command. When configured well, they map naturally to muscle memory and can be extremely fast to use.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Other pie-menu apps I've used include:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/pieoneer-multi-use-pie-menu"&gt;Pieoneer&lt;/a&gt; (good)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://apps.apple.com/us/app/cirmenu/id6450661015?mt=12"&gt;CirMenu&lt;/a&gt; (good)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/pie-menu"&gt;PieMenu&lt;/a&gt; (limited)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://kando.menu/"&gt;Kando&lt;/a&gt; (FOSS)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Interface&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In Radial, pie menus can include the following types of actions:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Input&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li class="lexxy-nested-listitem"&gt;&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Keyboard Shortcut&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Text&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Clipboard&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Open&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li class="lexxy-nested-listitem"&gt;&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Open App&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Open File&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Open URL&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Scripting&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li class="lexxy-nested-listitem"&gt;&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Apple Shortcut&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;AppleScript&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Shell Script&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Keyboard Maestro&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;System&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li class="lexxy-nested-listitem"&gt;&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Window Management&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;System Control&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The only obvious thing missing right now is deep-link support for tools like &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/how-to-get-the-most-from-raycast"&gt;Raycast&lt;/a&gt; and similar command launchers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Some Use Case Ideas&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Categorized Launchers&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Radial is much more than an &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;app launcher&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, but it works well for that role. You can create multiple menus and switch between them once a Radial menu is invoked with a keyboard shortcut or mouse gesture. One practical approach is to build menus around categories of apps you use regularly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Examples:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Browsers&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; – &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/safari-extensions-worth-paying-for-and-a-couple-of-worthy-freebies"&gt;Safari&lt;/a&gt;, Chrome, Firefox, Dia, &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/vivaldi-my-favorite-browser-just-got-some-updates"&gt;Vivaldi&lt;/a&gt;, Orion&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Utilities&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; – Emoji Picker, &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/why-haven-t-you-installed-keka-yet"&gt;Keka&lt;/a&gt;, PastePal, Updatest&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Writing&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; – &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/drafts-wins-app-of-the-year-at-mac-stories"&gt;Drafts&lt;/a&gt;, &lt;a href="https://obsidian.amerpie.lol/"&gt;Obsidian,&lt;/a&gt; LibreOffice, Dictionary&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Graphics&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; – &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/imageoptim-free-and-open-source-utility-to-reduce-file-sizes"&gt;ImageOptim&lt;/a&gt;, &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/consul-is-supremely-useful"&gt;Consul&lt;/a&gt;, Immich&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This kind of grouping works well because the direction of the slice becomes the memory trigger rather than the app name.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Consistent Application Menus&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Radial calls menus that are available everywhere &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;global menus&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;. It also supports &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;context-aware menus&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; that appear only in specific apps or groups of apps.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because Radial includes a template feature, you can create menus that behave consistently across your main working apps. Anything that can be triggered with a keyboard shortcut can live in the menu.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you place common commands in the same slice position across multiple apps, muscle memory kicks in quickly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Examples of commands that translate well across apps:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;New&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; – note, document, macro, shortcut, etc. (⌘N)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Settings&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; – quick access to preferences (⌘,)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Search / Search and Replace&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; (⌘F and ⌥⌘F)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You can still add app-specific commands; just keep their placement consistent so your muscle memory stays intact. I created Radial menus for Safari, &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/things-3-maybe-the-pinnacle-in-app-design"&gt;Things&lt;/a&gt;, Obsidian, and Drafts using this approach.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Automation Hub&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Where Radial really shines is as an &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;automation hub&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of launching apps individually, you can trigger an &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/enhance-apple-shortcuts-with-these-apps"&gt;Apple Shortcut&lt;/a&gt; or a &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/keyboard-maestro-the-app-that-makes-everything-better-tips-for-the-for-the-automation-curious"&gt;Keyboard Maestro&lt;/a&gt; macro that launches an entire workspace with a single click. A second action can close the same apps when you’re done.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you combine this with a window manager like &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/developer-spotlight-ryan-hanson"&gt;Rectangle&lt;/a&gt; or &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/snapsofapps-has-new-powerful-features"&gt;Snaps of Apps&lt;/a&gt;, you can go even further and &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;launch apps on specific displays and in specific Spaces with windows already arranged&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Another useful trick is reducing menu-bar clutter. Many utilities can have their core actions exposed through a Radial menu instead of living permanently in the menu bar.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Examples of apps that work well this way:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/cleanshot-x"&gt;CleanShot X&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Shortcuts&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Rectangle&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Keyboard Maestro&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Side Notes&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I also adapted my morning checklist into a Radial menu using a mix of actions:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Opening several daily websites in specific browsers&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Checking new email across three mailboxes&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Launching social media through the apps I actually use&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Opening &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/two-recommendations-for-syncing-utilities"&gt;Sync Folders Pro&lt;/a&gt; and &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/smartbackup-free-fast-and-foolproof"&gt;Smart Backup&lt;/a&gt; to verify my auto-archiving workflows for photos, music, ebooks, and video&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Sending a predefined prompt to ChatGPT that generates my daily report&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Logging into my self-hosted server for routine health checks&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Once it’s set up, everything can be accessed from a single menu instead of hunting through menus, booksmarks and other launchers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Details&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Privacy Policy&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Radial has a good privacy policy and you can read it at &lt;a href="https://radial.appverge.net/privacy"&gt;https://radial.appverge.net/privacy&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Radial includes a&lt;mark style="color:rgb(51, 61, 66);background-color:rgb(248, 248, 248);"&gt; built-in AI assistant using Meta's llama-3.1-8b-instant hosted on Groq (with a Q, not K).&lt;/mark&gt; Ideally, future versions will support additional providers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Radial is developed in Denmark, which means it falls under EU privacy regulations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Price&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Radial offers a seven-day free trial. The full license costs &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;€14.99&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; and covers &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;five seats&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, which is fairly generous for a utility in this category.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Website&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Radial’s website includes solid documentation and clear explanations of how the system works.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://radial.appverge.net/"&gt;Radial – Everything at Your Cursor&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="mailto:lou@louplummer.lol?subject=Radial%204%20Works%20Best%20as%20an%20Automation%20Hub" style="text-decoration: underline"&gt;✉️ Reply by email&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>
    <summary>I spent the afternoon experimenting with Radial 4, a rapidly evolving pie-menu app from independent developer Gustav Lubker of AppVerge. If you’re not familiar with pie menu apps, they present a circular menu divided into sections (or slices), each representing an action or command. When configured well, they map naturally to...</summary>

    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/15873</id>
    <published>2026-04-02T00:08:50Z</published>
    <updated>2026-04-02T07:29:10Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/backigo-is-a-dependable-full-featured-icloud-backup-solution"/>
    <title>BackiGo is a Dependable &amp; Full Featured iCloud Backup Solution</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--png"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" alt="BackiGo" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBeWFNQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--af2b5827c6f07fefea10231ba29f044b8b03abc9/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJY0c1bkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--768aeab7fb7843d85fe5b2b4ba237e06e6ef604f/SCR-20260401-rlxn.png" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
    &lt;figcaption class="attachment__caption text-center"&gt;
      BackiGo
    &lt;/figcaption&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you rely on iCloud but don’t have a true backup of that data, BackiGo is one of the simplest ways to create one.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://backigo.app/"&gt;BackiGo&lt;/a&gt; is an iCloud backup app I can recommend for anyone looking for an alternative to Parachute. Parachute is a well-known iCloud backup utility that was recently acquired by a company with a solid reputation, but also a history of price increases and subscription transitions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Who This Is For&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BackiGo is particularly useful if you:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Store large amounts of data in &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;iCloud Drive or iCloud Photos&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;
&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Use &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Optimize Mac Storage&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, meaning your Mac does not hold full local copies&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Want an &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;off-Apple backup copy&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; of your iCloud data&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Need to back up iCloud data to a &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;NAS, external drive, or another cloud provider&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;
&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why You Need an iCloud Backup&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Sometimes Apple’s logic escapes me. Nowhere is that more obvious than in the opaque world of iCloud.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you don’t have a method for keeping a &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;versioned backup of your iCloud documents and photos&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, you should set one up sooner rather than later.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The simplest approach looks like this:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Use a Mac signed into iCloud.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Turn &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;off&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; “Optimize Mac Storage” for both &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;iCloud Drive&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; and &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Photos&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Allow all files to download locally.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Let &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Time Machine&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; back up that Mac.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This works because Time Machine will keep historical versions of those files.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Unfortunately, that approach isn’t practical for everyone. If, like me, you pay for &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;2TB of iCloud storage&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; but your Mac has a much smaller internal drive that can’t be upgraded, downloading everything locally simply isn’t feasible.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Experienced Mac users already understand the core issue: &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;iCloud is a syncing service, not a backup.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you overwrite a file, the new version replaces the old one everywhere. If you delete a file, it disappears everywhere. If a file becomes corrupted, that corruption syncs too.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Even with Time Machine running, you still won’t have copies of many files if &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Optimize Mac Storage&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; is enabled, because those files never existed locally on your Mac.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The core idea is simple: &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;get a second copy of your iCloud data somewhere Apple’s sync engine can’t touch it.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One more thing - you can find multiple stories of people permanently losing access to their iCloud accounts through ID theft, malware and Apple’s own policies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;BackiGo Features&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where BackiGo comes in. The app lets you create a copy of your iCloud data and store it in a variety of locations:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;External drives (USB or Thunderbolt)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Other cloud providers with versioned storage, such as &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Dropbox&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; or &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Google Drive&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;
&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A NAS on your home network&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A shared folder on another computer (including Windows machines)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;An FTP server&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;WebDAV support is planned&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Some of the features I’ve found useful:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Universal app&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; that runs on Mac, iPhone, and iPad&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Flexible photo organization&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;; mirror your Apple Photos structure or export into folders by device/year/month (for example &lt;code&gt;AmerpieMBA/2026/04&lt;/code&gt;)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Selective backups&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;; back up documents but skip photos, or back up only specific albums&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Multiple cloud destinations&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, including Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, pCloud, and Backblaze&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Incremental and full backups&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Scheduled backups&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; based on time, frequency, and backup type&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Local Photos library support&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; for people who use Photos without iCloud&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Live Photo and shared album support&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Built-in photo viewer&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; to visually confirm what’s included in a backup&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Detailed reports&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; of backup and restore history, exportable as HTML or CSV&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Recent Updates&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Added backup encryption(optional).&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; While iCloud’s Advanced Data Protection (ADP) already encrypts data on Apple’s side, the app now adds client-side encryption, meaning your data is encrypted before it’s written to the backup destination. This helps protect your data even if the storage drive is lost, a cloud service is compromised, or an account gets leaked.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h4&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Also added iCloud archive restore support&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;: Restore iCloud Contacts and iCloud Drive documents Search your iCloud documents and restore specific files&lt;br&gt;
&lt;/h4&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Privacy Policy&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No data collected.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Developer Website&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://backigo.app/"&gt;BackiGo – Complete iCloud Photo backup and restore solution for iOS and Mac&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Price&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Free trial (limited to 500 images)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;$14.99 lifetime purchase&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;$6.99 annual subscription&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;$0.99 monthly subscription&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Available on the &lt;a href="https://apps.apple.com/us/app/backigo/id6746894565"&gt;Mac App Store&lt;/a&gt; with &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Family Sharing&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; enabled.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="mailto:lou@louplummer.lol?subject=BackiGo%20is%20a%20Dependable%20&amp;amp;%20Full%20Featured%20iCloud%20Backup%20Solution" style="text-decoration: underline"&gt;✉️ Reply by email&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>

If you rely on iCloud but don’t have a true backup of that data, BackiGo is one of the simplest ways to create one.

BackiGo is an iCloud backup app I can recommend for anyone looking for an alternative to Parachute. Parachute is a well-known iCloud backup utility that was...</summary>

  <entry>
    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/15845</id>
    <published>2026-03-30T19:06:39Z</published>
    <updated>2026-03-30T19:07:59Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/doublememory-doing-great-after-a-year"/>
    <title>DoubleMemory Doing Great After a Year</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;h1&gt;&lt;br&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" alt="DoubleMemory" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBOHlMQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--0fc05eaf09c15fe51b61f77821e44b4e6e6fdd9c/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJYW5CbkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--daf4078a1aefa3c961be2c7b8fbe4a74a2641c0c/CleanShot%202026-03-30%20at%2015.01.18.jpg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
    &lt;figcaption class="attachment__caption text-center"&gt;
      DoubleMemory
    &lt;/figcaption&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I’m always impressed when an out-of-the-box thinker builds an app unlike anything I’ve seen before. Iterating on proven concepts is fine, but after testing enough clipboard managers and voice-to-text apps, they all start to blur together. Give me something new, clever, &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;and&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; useful, and I’ll happily change my workflow to make room for it. a year ago, DoubleMemory caught my attention with its interesting feature set and it's done nothing but improve since then.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;&lt;a href="https://doublememory.com"&gt;DoubleMemory&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I sometimes worry that one day my brain will run out of capacity for new hotkey combinations. When that happens, any app that relies on them will be off the table. DoubleMemory neatly sidesteps that problem by baking the instruction directly into its name.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Press &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;⌘C twice quickly&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, and the app captures either the webpage you’re on or the text you’ve highlighted. It then drops that content into an aesthetically well-designed, searchable, Pinterest-like interface with some surprisingly useful capabilities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There’s a setting that allows DoubleMemory to save &lt;i&gt;&lt;em&gt;everything&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/i&gt; you copy, but I’d advise against leaving that on all the time. It’s not a clipboard manager in the sense that &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Raycast&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; or &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;PastePal&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; are. For example, it doesn’t capture images.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Where it shines is with URLs. Highlight the URL of any webpage you’re on and press &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;⌘C twice&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;. DoubleMemory downloads the page content and stores it locally, making it as much a &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;read-it-later tool&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; as a bookmark manager. In practice, it works well as either.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Saved content can sync via &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;iCloud&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, which means your collection is accessible on your iPhone, iPad, and other Macs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;DoubleMemory also doubles as a lightweight notes tool. Highlight a passage of text anywhere, press &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;⌘C twice&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, and it’s saved to your board. From there you can add your own commentary and organize the entry with tags. There’s even optional &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;AI-powered auto-tagging&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; if you want help categorizing things.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One detail I appreciate: &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;DoubleMemory doesn’t require an account&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, and you don’t need to install a browser extension. If you routinely save URLs from different sources on a specific topic, you quickly end up with a clean, searchable database that works offline.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It’s also refreshingly lightweight. The app uses roughly &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;10 MB of RAM&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; during normal use. For automation fans, it supports &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Apple Shortcuts&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, the &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;macOS share sheet&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, and &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;drag-and-drop to the Dock&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; (if you enable the Dock icon).&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Interesting Features&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Bookmark Imports&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;If you want to migrate an existing read-it-later list or bookmarks from another service (for example &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Raindrop&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;), DoubleMemory includes solid import tools.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Active Roadmap&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;I’ve been following the project for about a year, and development has been steady. Planned features include &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;image and screenshot support&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; and &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;automated imports of saved searches&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;. Personally, I’d love to see it pull in my saved Reddit posts.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Approachable Developer&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;The developer is easy to reach and actively engages with users. There’s a &lt;a href="https://discord.gg/6REDWJuRy4"&gt;Discord&lt;/a&gt;, a &lt;a href="https://doublememory.substack.com/"&gt;Substack&lt;/a&gt; newsletter, an active Reddit presence, and a well-maintained website with an up-to-date changelog.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Freemium Model&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;The free tier already allows unlimited saves, notes, bookmarks, and tags. The Pro plan mainly adds more than three saved searches and supports the developer. Future premium features are expected to focus on &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;advanced retrieval, AI-powered organization, and richer content consumption tools&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;. I have some 50% off subscription codes. Use the comment tool below if you want one.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;DoubleMemory has a lot going for it. It’s easy to understand, genuinely useful in daily workflows, and feature-rich without feeling bloated.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="mailto:lou@louplummer.lol?subject=DoubleMemory%20Doing%20Great%20After%20a%20Year" style="text-decoration: underline"&gt;✉️ Reply by email&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>
    <summary>

I’m always impressed when an out-of-the-box thinker builds an app unlike anything I’ve seen before. Iterating on proven concepts is fine, but after testing enough clipboard managers and voice-to-text apps, they all start to blur together. Give me something new, clever, and useful, and I’ll happily change my workflow...</summary>

    <title>500 App Reviews Published!</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--png"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" alt="Number 500!!!" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBMXVMQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--4d2220436baeb2b7e6562eda2909b792c74afd9c/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJY0c1bkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--768aeab7fb7843d85fe5b2b4ba237e06e6ef604f/appaddict500.png" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
    &lt;figcaption class="attachment__caption text-center"&gt;
      Number 500!!!
    &lt;/figcaption&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I posted my 500th app review this week. If you keep typing long enough, this is what happens. It makes me super happy and I hope I have helped some of you find apps that you've grown to use and love. If I have, please leave a comment, it will be motivating and appreciated. I want to give a shout out to &lt;a href="https://reddit.com/r/macapps"&gt; r/MacApps&lt;/a&gt; for all the support and feedback I've gotten there. I also want to thank &lt;a href="https://scribbles.page"&gt;Scribbles&lt;/a&gt;, the blogging platform I've used the entire time.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I recently added a way for developers to alert me to their apps. If you know anyone who has an app that could use some exposure, please let them know they can request a review &lt;a href="https://www.cognitoforms.com/AppAddictapp/AppReviewSubmission"&gt;here&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AppAddict is just me, one old guy with a laptop and a decades old predilection for clicking the download button on just about every app I see. This is my hobby, not a side job. I do it because I enjoy it. I can't tell you how thrilling it's been to interact with developers of some of my favorite apps. I still have a big streak of fanboy.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" alt="Analytics" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBMTZMQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--cbf948cf1311d42e52ab8c64406de369b1052ea3/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJYW5CbkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--daf4078a1aefa3c961be2c7b8fbe4a74a2641c0c/CleanShot%202026-03-29%20at%2006.28.16.jpg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;

  <entry>
    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/15789</id>
    <published>2026-03-27T01:46:14Z</published>
    <updated>2026-03-27T01:46:16Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/automation-fans-are-going-to-love-picmal-for-conversions"/>
    <title>Automation Fans Are Going to Love PicMal for Conversions</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" alt="PicMal" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBOUNLQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--bb58781cc3899738a2935f6036e470520ff9197b/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJYW5CbkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--daf4078a1aefa3c961be2c7b8fbe4a74a2641c0c/CleanShot%202026-03-26%20at%2021.42.00.jpg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
    &lt;figcaption class="attachment__caption text-center"&gt;
      PicMal
    &lt;/figcaption&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Every Mac user eventually ends up with a pile of files that need converting. Screenshots that are too large for the web. HEIC photos from iPhones that need to become JPEGs. Audio recordings saved at ridiculous bitrates. Video files that need to be optimized for sharing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You can solve all of that with command-line tools like &lt;code&gt;ffmpeg&lt;/code&gt; or with a handful of separate utilities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Or you can just use &lt;a href="https://picmal.app/"&gt;Picmal&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Picmal is a single macOS utility that handles image, audio, and video conversion and compression. Once installed, it integrates directly into the &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Dock, Finder, menu bar, Services, and Shortcuts,&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; so it behaves more like a built-in system tool than a typical standalone app.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It works immediately with sensible defaults, but if you want to tweak codecs, formats, or compression levels, the controls are there.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Images&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I’ve set up one of my screenshot apps specifically for images I plan to post on the web. It saves those screenshots into a folder that Picmal watches.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When a file lands there, Picmal automatically:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;converts it to my preferred format&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;applies a compression level that keeps good clarity while shrinking the file size&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;renames the file so I know it’s already been processed&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That automation alone has been useful for blogging and documentation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you regularly deal with HEIC photos from iPhones or iPads, Picmal can also watch a folder and convert them automatically.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Picmal also handles image resizing and color space conversion (sRGB, ProPhoto RGB, Display P3, and others). If you’re preparing files for printing, you can adjust DPI as well.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Audio&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Batch processing works well. I had a collection of spoken-word recordings from events I’d attended, and many of them had been saved at extremely high bitrates that made sense for music but not for speech.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Picmal converted and compressed the entire batch without complaint. The resulting files sounded the same for spoken content while taking up far less disk space.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Video&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Video conversion uses simple presets:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Maximum Quality&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Balanced (Size &amp;amp; Quality)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Web Optimized&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Social Media&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Maximum Compression&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Custom&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Pick the preset that matches the destination and you’re done. If you need more control, the Custom option exposes additional settings.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Clipboard Optimization&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Clipboard optimization lets Picmal compress images you copy to the clipboard. Copy a screenshot, a web image, or a file in Finder and Picmal quietly optimizes it in the background.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A small overlay appears so you can immediately replace the original clipboard contents with the compressed version.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you enable the option, Picmal can automatically copy the optimized image back to your clipboard. One practical advantage: images processed this way can be pasted into Finder as files, which isn’t something macOS normally allows with clipboard images.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A nice touch: if the image is already efficiently compressed, Picmal detects that and skips the process instead of recompressing it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How It Fits Into a Typical Mac Workflow&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you already use media tools on macOS, you might be wondering where Picmal fits.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/imageoptim-free-and-open-source-utility-to-reduce-file-sizes"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;ImageOptim&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;Great for compressing images, especially for web publishing. Picmal overlaps here but adds format conversion, automation via watched folders, and clipboard workflows.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/permute-powerful-easy-to-use-media-converter-for-images-video-and-audio"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Permute &lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;Permute focuses mostly on media conversion with a clean UI. Picmal covers similar ground but adds automation features and deeper Finder integration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FFmpeg"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;ffmpeg / command-line tools&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;Still the most flexible option for scripting and complex workflows. Picmal obviously can’t match that level of control, but for everyday tasks it removes a lot of friction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In practice, Picmal feels less like a replacement for those tools and more like a convenient layer on top of common conversion tasks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Final Thoughts&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At $15.99 per seat with lifetime updates, Picmal is reasonably priced for what it does. There’s also a 15-day no-questions-asked refund.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;All processing happens locally on your Mac (macOS 14 or newer), and the developer states that no data is collected. If you want to dig deeper, the developer provides &lt;a href="https://picmal.app/docs"&gt;comprehensive documentation&lt;/a&gt; on the website.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="mailto:lou@louplummer.lol?subject=Automation%20Fans%20Are%20Going%20to%20Love%20PicMal%20for%20Conversions" style="text-decoration: underline"&gt;✉️ Reply by email&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>
    <summary>Every Mac user eventually ends up with a pile of files that need converting. Screenshots that are too large for the web. HEIC photos from iPhones that need to become JPEGs. Audio recordings saved at ridiculous bitrates. Video files that need to be optimized for sharing.

You can solve all...</summary>

  <entry>
    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/15762</id>
    <published>2026-03-25T20:22:29Z</published>
    <updated>2026-03-25T20:22:31Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/10-tiny-mac-workflow-tweaks-that-save-me-time-every-day"/>
    <title>10 Tiny Mac Workflow Tweaks that Save Me Time Every Day</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpeg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" alt="Power User Apps" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBeWFLQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--ce4121c53d071566c797687a8531c3d4747b1daa/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lKYW5CbFp3WTZCa1ZVT2hSeVpYTnBlbVZmZEc5ZmJHbHRhWFJiQjJrQ0FBaHBBZ0FHT2dwellYWmxjbnNIT2dwemRISnBjRlE2REhGMVlXeHBkSGxwWkE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoidmFyaWF0aW9uIn19--fa3dbe24e376882dfd8c9dddfec0441143a8bd41/a_3x4_grid_of_application_icons_is_displayed_on_a.jpeg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
    &lt;figcaption class="attachment__caption text-center"&gt;
      Power User Apps
    &lt;/figcaption&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I spend a lot of time trying to remove small bits of friction from my Mac workflow. macOS is a great system, but out of the box it still leaves a lot of obvious automation opportunities on the table.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I spend a lot of time trying to remove small bits of friction from my Mac workflow. macOS is a great system, but out of the box it still leaves a lot of obvious automation opportunities on the table.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Most of the improvements I rely on come from stitching together tools like AppleScript, Keyboard Maestro, Shortcuts, and a few power-user utilities I discovered at &lt;a href="https://reddit.com/r/macapps"&gt;r/MacApps&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;None of this is complicated once it’s set up. The goal is just to eliminate little interruptions that happen dozens of times a day.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Here are a few small automations and workflow tweaks that currently make my Mac feel a lot more like &lt;i&gt;&lt;em&gt;my&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/i&gt; machine.&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;I like Safari, but I don’t like how easily it spawns extra windows. I now use an &lt;a href="https://dropover.cloud/42839b"&gt;AppleScript&lt;/a&gt; tied to &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/keyboard-maestro-the-app-that-makes-everything-better-tips-for-the-for-the-automation-curious"&gt;Keyboard Maestro&lt;/a&gt;. With a mouse click or hotkey, it closes every Safari window except the frontmost one.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Safari has good AppleScript and Shortcuts support, but it still doesn’t provide a keyboard-friendly way to jump directly to a specific Tab Group. My workaround is &lt;a href="https://www.icloud.com/shortcuts/424633ecabef49bba903e3f03b68bc62"&gt;an Apple Shortcut that batch-opens groups of URLs&lt;/a&gt; that mirror my tab groups: Server, Social, Blogging, Software, etc.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;I set up &lt;a href="https://folivora.ai/"&gt;BetterTouchTool&lt;/a&gt; so that &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;fn + Button 3&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; on my Logitech mouse triggers the &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;New&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; command across roughly two dozen apps. Depending on the app, that can mean a new tab, new note, new document, new Shortcut, new Keyboard Maestro macro, new email, or new message.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;I’m currently using &lt;a href="https://www.apptorium.com/sidenotes"&gt;SideNotes&lt;/a&gt; as my scratchpad. It stays hidden on the right edge of my primary display until I toggle it with a hotkey or an &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/extra-bar-gets-extra-features"&gt;ExtraBar&lt;/a&gt; menu item.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Most of these are tiny things, but they add up surprisingly fast&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;I use &lt;a href="https://github.com/rxhanson/RectanglePro-Community/discussions/111"&gt;Rectangle Pro’s layout manager&lt;/a&gt; to launch and arrange &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;10 apps across two displays and eight virtual desktops&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;. Each desktop has a keyboard shortcut, and I tie them together with a single Keyboard Maestro macro. &lt;a href="https://dropover.cloud/bda645"&gt;(download link)&lt;/a&gt;
&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;I wrote a small shell script &lt;a href="https://dropover.cloud/85439b"&gt;(download link)&lt;/a&gt; that reconnects me to &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/ailscale-the-best-free-app-most-mac-power-users-aren-t-using"&gt;Tailscale&lt;/a&gt; if the connection drops or fails to start. It runs via &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;launchd&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, configured through &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/stop-making-cron-jobs"&gt;Lingon Pro&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;I use macOS 26’s automation features in Apple Shortcuts to create my daily Obsidian note from a template. The automation also inserts a weather report and the day’s calendar events, so the note is ready when I sit down at my desk each morning. (Requires &lt;a href="https://apps.apple.com/us/app/actions-for-obsidian/id1659667937"&gt;Actions for Obsidian&lt;/a&gt;.)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;When I need a dual-pane file manager instead of Finder, a Keyboard Maestro trigger runs an AppleScript that closes all Finder windows and replaces them with a ForkLift window. (&lt;a href="https://a.dropoverapp.com/cloud/download/c4376cdb-9bd3-4a1e-be1e-e8b79d139155/2b0a6331-f55c-406d-ab56-18d0d82cbf11"&gt;download macro&lt;/a&gt;)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;I removed the menu bar icons for &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/better-touch-tool-favoriteso"&gt;BetterTouchTool&lt;/a&gt;, &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/default-folder-x-an-og-app-for-mac-power-users"&gt;Default Folder X&lt;/a&gt;, &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/using-supercharge"&gt;Supercharge&lt;/a&gt;, and Rectangle Pro. Their functions are now exposed through ExtraBar instead.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;If a developer doesn’t expose a URL scheme, you can’t deep-link into specific menu items. Finder is a good example; there’s no direct link for &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Go to Folder&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;. ExtraBar can run scripts, though, so a small AppleScript can send keystrokes to trigger the command. If the feature exists in a menu but has no keyboard shortcut, you can also create your own under &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Sample Script&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;tell application "Finder"&lt;/code&gt;&lt;br&gt;&lt;code&gt;activate&lt;/code&gt;&lt;br&gt;&lt;code&gt;end tell&lt;/code&gt;&lt;br&gt;&lt;code&gt;tell application "System Events"&lt;/code&gt;&lt;br&gt;&lt;code&gt;keystroke "g" using {command down, shift down}&lt;/code&gt;&lt;br&gt;&lt;code&gt;end tell&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;hr&gt;

&lt;p&gt;None of these are huge changes individually, but together they remove a lot of small interruptions during the day.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Curious what small automations or workflow tricks other people here are using.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="mailto:lou@louplummer.lol?subject=10%20Tiny%20Mac%20Workflow%20Tweaks%20that%20Save%20Me%20Time%20Every%20Day" style="text-decoration: underline"&gt;✉️ Reply by email&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>
    <summary>I spend a lot of time trying to remove small bits of friction from my Mac workflow. macOS is a great system, but out of the box it still leaves a lot of obvious automation opportunities on the table.

I spend a lot of time trying to remove small bits...</summary>

  <entry>
    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/15736</id>
    <published>2026-03-24T15:40:46Z</published>
    <updated>2026-03-24T15:40:48Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/consul-is-supremely-useful"/>
    <title>Consul is Supremely Useful</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" alt="Automation" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBK21KQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--46c431fc5cc6baa73f13cc6be141c3b47829cc8d/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJYW5CbkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--daf4078a1aefa3c961be2c7b8fbe4a74a2641c0c/CleanShot%202026-03-24%20at%2011.40.00.jpg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
    &lt;figcaption class="attachment__caption text-center"&gt;
      Automation
    &lt;/figcaption&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I’ve become quite fond of &lt;a href="https://getconsul.app/"&gt;Consul&lt;/a&gt;, a relatively new file conversion utility that’s both simple to use and easy to automate. The concept is almost absurdly straightforward: change the file extension to the format you want and the conversion just happens.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You might think you’ll never really need to convert files from one format to another. In practice, that assumption tends to collapse sooner or later. A few situations I’ve run into over the years:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Switching from one e-reader (for example, Sony) to another (Kindle) and suddenly needing to convert an entire library of books.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;My photography workflow revolves around Canon’s RAW format (CR2). When a relative passed away and I inherited his photo archive, the files were a mix of several other RAW formats.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;After living through the minor apocalypse when Microsoft killed Works, you’d think I would have learned something about proprietary formats. Instead, I spent another twenty years writing in Word before finally switching to Markdown.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Occasionally grabbing an iPhone photo and realizing it exported as HEIC, which remains incompatible with far more things than it should be.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Optimizing photos and video for my blog or social media.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are plenty of ways to convert files. Most of them involve some level of friction:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Opening an app (Word, for example) and using &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;File → Save As&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; to create another copy in a different format.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Uploading files to random conversion websites with unclear privacy policies.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Using powerful utilities like &lt;a href="https://software.charliemonroe.net/permute/"&gt;Permute&lt;/a&gt;, which are excellent but come with a bit of a learning curve.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Building your own workflow with Apple Shortcuts if you enjoy assembling that kind of plumbing.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;What makes Consul such a pleasure is the complete absence of friction. It runs quietly in the background, and when you need to convert something, it just happens the moment you rename the file. For most conversions, the default settings are fine, but in the settings, you can control exactly how each conversion is handled including the output quality and codec, or whether to strip metadata.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Mac automation nerds, Consul can be set to watch folders and perform conversions when a certain file type lands there. You can use Consul with &lt;a href="https://amerpie.lol/2024/05/10/my-favorite-actions.html"&gt;Hazel&lt;/a&gt; or another automation tool like &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/developer-spotlight-low-tech-guys-maker-of-clop-lunar-rcmd-pipiri-and-crank"&gt;Crank&lt;/a&gt; to route the converted file elsewhere, import it into Photos or upload it to an FTP server.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Consul currently supports &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;1,391 conversions across 76 file formats&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, covering images, audio, video, documents, e-books, email, configuration files, spreadsheets, and archives.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The developer’s site suggests more formats are planned. I’d particularly like to see support for Apple iWork files and OpenOffice spreadsheets and presentations. My pie-in-the-sky request would be a &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;PDF → EPUB conversion&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; that performs better than what Calibre currently produces.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Pricing is refreshingly simple. A single license is &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;$14&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, and a three-seat license is &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;$19&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, both including a year of updates.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The privacy policy is exactly what you want to see: &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;no data collection&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;. Email support is available, and the developer is &lt;a href="https://www.reddit.com/user/Spaaze/"&gt;active on Reddit&lt;/a&gt; and notably friendly when people have questions.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="mailto:lou@louplummer.lol?subject=Consul%20is%20Supremely%20Useful" style="text-decoration: underline"&gt;✉️ Reply by email&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>
    <summary>I’ve become quite fond of Consul, a relatively new file conversion utility that’s both simple to use and easy to automate. The concept is almost absurdly straightforward: change the file extension to the format you want and the conversion just happens.

You might think you’ll never really need to convert files...</summary>

      <name>Lou Plummer</name>
      <uri>https://appaddict.app</uri>

  <entry>
    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/15705</id>
    <published>2026-03-22T14:17:16Z</published>
    <updated>2026-03-22T14:17:17Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/if-these-apps-are-missing-my-mac-feels-broken"/>
    <title>If These Apps Are Missing My Mac Feels Broken</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;Some small utilities become so embedded in my workflow that they start to feel like part of macOS itself. When I sit down at someone else’s Mac or a freshly set-up machine and they aren’t there, it genuinely throws me off.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I’m curious what apps fall into that category for you.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Shareful&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBMU9KQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--2f7290055972ec9ef48a13962080bc65a34f6b1f/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJYW5CbkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--daf4078a1aefa3c961be2c7b8fbe4a74a2641c0c/screenshot1.Cu-zFadA.jpg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of those apps for me is &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/shareful-a-free-app-i-use-every-day"&gt;Shareful&lt;/a&gt; by &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/the-many-apps-of-sindre-sorhus"&gt;Sindre Sorhus&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Mac share menu has always felt like an afterthought compared to iOS. Many developers don’t bother implementing it, and Apple keeps it oddly limited. Shareful fixes that by adding a few practical actions that save me a surprising number of clicks every day:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Copy&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Open In&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Save As…&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Save to Downloads&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It’s simple, but once you have it, the default share sheet feels incomplete without it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Start by Innovative Bytes&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBMVNKQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--31cbb665d0bc6bf98debaacfdad43d3f1b554887/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJYW5CbkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--daf4078a1aefa3c961be2c7b8fbe4a74a2641c0c/start.jpg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Even though I’m very much a keyboard-launcher person (Team &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/how-to-get-the-most-from-raycast"&gt;Raycast&lt;/a&gt;), there are situations where that approach breaks down.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Sometimes I need a small, obscure utility whose name I can’t remember. When your &lt;code&gt;/Applications&lt;/code&gt; folder is as crowded as mine, scrolling through it isn’t realistic.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That’s where &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/start-from-innovative-bytes"&gt;Start from Innovative Bytes&lt;/a&gt; comes in. Two features make it especially useful.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Tagging&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;Tagging lets you create categories for apps without any friction. You can even nest them, like &lt;code&gt;Utilities/Screenshots&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;Utilities/Clipboard&lt;/code&gt;, which makes browsing a large app library much more manageable.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Notes&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;You can attach a short description to an app so you remember what it actually does.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A good example is the file-conversion utility &lt;a href="https://getconsul.app/"&gt;Consul&lt;/a&gt;, which lets you change an image’s format just by renaming it. Seeing a note like “file rename / conversion” when browsing makes it much easier to find again later.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Honorable Mentions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/apparency-the-app-that-open-apps"&gt;Apparency – The App That Opens Apps&lt;/a&gt; — a Quick Look extension and inspection utility for applications&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/cleanshot-x"&gt;CleanShot X&lt;/a&gt; — the screenshot tool whose keyboard shortcuts are permanently burned into my muscle memory; although &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/screenfloat-is-a-different-kind-of-screenshot-app"&gt;ScreenFloat&lt;/a&gt; is starting to make a case for itself&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="mailto:lou@louplummer.lol?subject=If%20These%20Apps%20Are%20Missing%20My%20Mac%20Feels%20Broken" style="text-decoration: underline"&gt;✉️ Reply by email&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>
    <summary>Some small utilities become so embedded in my workflow that they start to feel like part of macOS itself. When I sit down at someone else’s Mac or a freshly set-up machine and they aren’t there, it genuinely throws me off.

I’m curious what apps fall into that category for...</summary>
